newsitem.title: CANADA: Dry Australian barley fields may buoy prices - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Dry Australian barley fields may buoy prices - CWB.

text.p: Dry soil conditions in the last month before Australia's barley harvest may reduce output and raise world feed and malt barley prices, the Canadian Wheat Board's director of weather and crop surveillance said.

"If the Australian barley crop is at all reduced, it'll have a big impact on us both in terms of feeding and malting barley because they're a major competitor for us," the CWB's Paul Bullock said at Manitoba Pool Elevators' annual meeting.
The CWB reduced its world feed barley price forecast by C$7 a tonne last month to the C$143-$163 a tonne in benchmark No1 Canada Western Feed Barley.

What pressured prices in the past month was a larger world coarse grain production estimate by the International Grains Council on Oct 24 at 875 million tonnes and the European Union's resumption of export subsidies last month.
But a reduction in Australia's output may buoy prices.

The Australian Wheat Forecasters firm on Oct 21 said it expected Australian barley production from the current harvest at 6.14 million tonnes, but the CWB's Bullock said he expects 6.0 million tonnes.
Southern Australia received half of its normal rainfall amounts in the last month, Bullock said.

"Victoria and south Australia is where the big barley growing areas are. That harvest, which just started - it's these next three, four weeks that's going to make or break it," Bullock told reporters after a speech to MPE delegates.
"It's been dry and that may cut into the yields but that's positive for quality if it stays that way," he added.
Rainfall in Australia's wheat belt was normal to above normal and Bullock concurred with the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Nov 12 output estimate of 21 million tonnes.
